episode_title: True Wealth: Building Business Success Without Sacrificing Your Life feat. Kelsey Kitsch

real_qa.q: How does Kelsey Kitsch connect intimate relationships with spouse to business success and entrepreneurial performance?
real_qa.r: Kelsey explains that when your primary relationship is strong and stable, you have more courage at work, more focus, and more enthusiasm—feeling unstoppable. However, business success does not automatically translate to relationship success. She emphasizes that having a robust relationship foundation is more impactful for building great businesses than most realize, and that the strongest relationships at the start can become perilous long-term if neglected while pursuing career growth.
real_qa.requete: how intimate relationships affect business success

real_qa.q: What is the difference between being rich and wealthy according to Kelsey Kitsch's experience?
real_qa.r: Kelsey describes being rich but not wealthy as having financial success while sacrificing other life domains. She shared that after having her first child on a Friday, she returned to work Monday with the infant living in a crib in her office desk for the first year. She realized she had lost her humanity and become 'a robot'—executing strategy but missing the personal parts of herself that originally sparked her entrepreneurial drive, making wealth hollow without life integration.

real_qa.q: Why did Kelsey Kitsch decline Canada's number one female entrepreneur award a third time?
real_qa.r: Kelsey explained that integrity is her number one mantra and she was offered the award a third time but declined it because it wasn't making way for anyone else and had become distracting. She felt that chasing external metrics and jumping through hoops for awards no longer served her growth, and her real growth edge lay in examining the personal parts of herself she had shut down to show up as a business person.
real_qa.requete: Kelsey Kitsch Canada entrepreneur award declined

real_qa.q: How does AI productivity advantage require human wisdom and strategy to be effective?
real_qa.r: Kelsey uses a golf analogy to explain that if you are off by 1% at the moment you strike the ball over 500 yards, you end up quite a distance from the pin. She argues that deploying AI without the right prompts, direction, and strategy results in 'a whole lot of gobbledygook' and useless information. The true differentiator is wisdom—earned experience and unique perspective—which AI cannot provide; AI can give stats but not wisdom.

real_qa.q: What cancer diagnosis survival rate changed Kelsey Kitsch's perspective on success and time allocation?
real_qa.r: Kelsey was diagnosed with cancer when her third child was two months old, with a 17% survival rate prognosis. This diagnosis made 'the room close in' and everything become clear—she realized she had only one ride on Earth and imagined her funeral, recognizing that being remembered only for work until age twenty and then working constantly did not align with her values. This prompted her to redefine success to include aliveness, relationships, and whole-life value alongside financial accomplishment.

guest.entreprise: Multiple ventures (civil infrastructure, toys, psychedelic drug development, intimacy intelligence)
guest.bio_context: Kelsey Kitsch was twice named Canada's number one female entrepreneur and has built multi-million dollar companies. She raised $38 million and took a company public. She authored the book Success Hangover. She has built businesses spanning civil infrastructure (roads, bridges, dams), children's toys, psychedelic drug development, and intimacy intelligence. She was diagnosed with cancer with a 17% survival rate, which became a pivotal moment in redefining her approach to business and life integration.

real_quote: The wisdom is our earned experience, our own unique perspective, that thing that makes us us. AI can give you stats, but it's not going to give you wisdom.
